Speed work (PR #133, 2026-10-31) was measured on a production build (`next build && next start`), not `next dev`; dev compile time makes every page look slow.

- QA workspace is empty after `--reset`; seed it by importing a Revolut-format CSV (recognized without AI, so no model call needed).
- React `cache()` does not memoize in route handlers (chat, artifact frame): use `lib/per-client.ts` for per-request sharing there.
- `requireWorkspace()` runs again on every call inside route handlers; chat route tests deliberately pin the extra scope re-checks, so don't remove them.
- `staleTimes.dynamic` was tried and reverted: back navigation to pages older than the stale time re-renders them (Home back 34 ms to 886 ms); with 0, back is always instant.
- Pre-launch: the user allows breaking old artifacts/data for speed (2026-11-01).

input.title: Faster desktop cold start
input.task:
Repo: Moneo, an Electron desktop app (desktop/) that on launch starts bundled Postgres, GoTrue, Storage API, PostgREST, a gateway, then a Next.js standalone server, then opens the window. Read AGENTS.md (especially "Desktop app") and desktop/README.md, desktop/src/backend/README.md first, and follow AGENTS.md (no comments, surgical changes, commit each step).

Goal: make the time from double-clicking Moneo (app closed, and after a reboot = cold disk cache) until the Home page is usable as short as possible, and the app lighter (memory, processes). Measure first, then fix, commit by commit.

Measure: `node scripts/desktop/fetch-backend.mjs --platform win-x64` once, `npm run desktop:build`, then run with `MONEO_DESKTOP_HOME` set to a scratch folder (NEVER the owner's real user-data folder or installed app). Add timestamps from the logs (desktop/src/paths.ts log, backend.log) for each phase: electron ready, port, certificate, postgres start, each service ready, migrations check, owner creation, Next server ready (/api/health), window first paint, Home rendered. Do both a first run and a second (normal) start. `npm run desktop:smoke` exists too.

Known candidates in desktop/src/main.ts and desktop/src/backend/index.ts:
- auth (GoTrue), storage and rest (PostgREST) start strictly one after another; they only need Postgres. Start them concurrently; start the Next server as soon as its env is known (ports can be chosen up front) instead of after the whole backend + owner step.
- ensureBankCertificate runs serially before the backend; move it off the critical path if it can.
- createOwner / migrationState / revokeMigrationOwners / ALTER ROLE run every start; skip work already done (config.json knows schemaVersion etc.) while still detecting real changes.
- waitFor polling intervals; Next readiness polls every 250 ms.
- Next server cold start: try Node's compile cache (module.enableCompileCache / NODE_COMPILE_CACHE in a folder under the Moneo home) for the utilityProcess and the storage fork; measure.
- Show the window (or the setup screen) immediately and load Home as soon as Next is ready; check the first page request isn't slowed by on-demand compilation or cold DB caches.
- Postgres settings for a single-user desktop (shared_buffers, fsync is NOT allowed to be turned off — data safety first), GoTrue/Storage memory.
Keep data safety: pre-upgrade backup, migrations and error reporting must still work exactly. Keep security fuses.

Report a before/after table per phase. Open a PR with `gh pr create --base t3/speed-build-and-startup` (NOT main), with the numbers and a Speed section. Run npm test, npm run lint, npm run typecheck before. Last line: PR <url>, head <sha>, checks <state>.

I've landed four speed fixes on `t3/speed-build-and-startup` and opened draft PR [#318](https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo/pull/318) to merge it into main later. Its full CI run passed. Two subagents are still working in their own worktrees and will open PRs into this branch.

**What changed:**

| Change | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `next build` no longer runs its own type check; `npm run typecheck` already does, and now runs `next typegen` first so route types are still checked | local build 50 s (TypeScript phase 101 s from cold) | local build 23 s |
| CI dependency cache is keyed on the lockfile only, so editing an npm script no longer forces a full `npm ci` (50–80 s per job) | build 165 s, browser 248 s, test 105 s | build 34 s, browser 109 s, test 29 s |
| Session tokens are checked on the server with `JWT_SECRET` instead of a call to the auth service (about 60 ms, twice per page). The desktop app now passes `JWT_SECRET` to its Next server. | time to first byte ~95 ms | ~35 ms |
| The Claude Code library loads only when a Claude model actually runs, not on every cold start | about 150 ms of compiling at start-up | gone from start-up |

The token change also cuts the full Accounts render from 207 ms to 118 ms; every page, action and API call gains about the same. The CI numbers before the change come from a run where the cache missed, so part of that gain is the restored cache. CI's slowest jobs are now typecheck (68 s) and browser (109 s).

**Tried and dropped, because they didn't help:**
- Turning off Next's preloading of every page at start-up made no measurable difference.
- Raising the data API's connection pool from 10 to 40 was within noise.
- Starting the background-job runtime without waiting for it would have saved about 250 ms on the first request. I left it alone because an existing test deliberately requires start-up to wait for it.

**What's still slow:**
- **First page after the server starts:** Home takes 2–3 s, against 0.6 s when warm. Most of that is Node compiling code on start-up. Node's compile cache could fix it, but it only saves on a clean exit, so it suits the desktop app. That's part of the desktop subagent's task.
- **Home on the server:** about 80 database queries in three waves, with roughly 100 ms of computing in between. That's the next piece of work to hand out.
- **Dev server:** about 18 s to start from cold, 6.5 s for the first Home page. Loading `next.config.ts` takes 10 s on a cold disk.

This machine is running several other Docker stacks, so every timing is noisy and I repeated runs before trusting any number.

**Running now:**
- [Faster typecheck and lint](t3-thread://v2/88042f69-c439-49f6-a4b9-1fb5180f2502/thread:delegated-task:command%3Amcp%3A69847fef-da96-4810-b2ac-2bb541d41be3%3Adelegate-task%3A7b0ae64f-dc6f-4fd3-b279-29fe36effdfc) (gpt-6.2-sol): trying the native TypeScript compiler, oxlint and ESLint caching.

**Next, as slots free up (two at a time):** the Home query waterfall, Moneo's own time before the first chat reply (with the AI mocked), and dev-server start-up.

- To log the query waterfall temporarily, wrap supabaseFetch in lib/supabase-fetch.ts with timing console.log (do not commit that).

**Build and checks**
- `next build` no longer runs its own type check, which only repeated `npm run typecheck`. `typecheck` now runs `next typegen` first, so route types are still checked.
- Type checking uses the native TypeScript 7 compiler for the app and desktop projects. The three checks run in parallel and keep incremental caches in CI (#319). Injected type, indexed-access, lint and feature-map errors still fail.
- Lint prechecks run without nested npm start-up. The feature map scans the source in one pass.
- The CI `node_modules` cache is keyed on the lockfile only, so editing an npm script no longer forces `npm ci` (50–80 s) in every job. A cache miss now installs from the npm download cache.

**Every request**
- The backend signs session tokens with HS256. Supabase's `getClaims()` therefore called GoTrue `/auth/v1/user` (~60 ms) in the proxy and again in `requireWorkspace` on every page, action and API call. The token's signature is now checked on the server with `JWT_SECRET`. A token that fails the check still goes to GoTrue, and `requireWorkspace` still confirms the user with GoTrue once a minute. The desktop app passes `JWT_SECRET` to its Next server.
- The Claude Code provider and agent SDK load only when a Claude model runs, so they're no longer compiled on every server start.

**Home and chat (#321)**
- The Home heading streams on its own. Independent widget reads start earlier, and loan, budget and agent-run data is shared within one render (71 → 68 queries).
- Money and date formatters are reused instead of rebuilt for every figure. Output is identical: rendered figures matched the previous build in all eight default widgets, on desktop and mobile.
- Chat starts its read-only setup alongside creating the conversation. Attachment parsers and optional modules load only when used, and title generation starts once the answer is under way.

**Desktop start (#320)**
- GoTrue, Storage and PostgREST start together once Postgres is up. The Next server and the bank certificate start as soon as the ports are chosen. Readiness checks every 50 ms instead of 250 ms.
- In the desktop app, background work (workflow recovery, scheduler, bank listener) waits for a `moneo:backend-ready` message. The message is sent again if the Next server restarts. The source install is unchanged.

- Turning off Next's preloading of every page at start-up: no faster on the source install, and on desktop the first visit to each other page became 0.2–0.4 s slower.

def frames_for(label, title, min_gap):

Home now opens about 1 s before file storage is ready, and Moneo reopens in about 2.5 s instead of 6.4 s. If storage fails it restarts once by itself; a second failure shows the error screen. Both changes, the page speed-ups the stopped subagent had left behind, and the recordings are now in [#318](https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo/pull/318). Its CI is running on the latest push, and I haven't merged it to main.

**Storage start-up**
- On a normal reopen, Home appears about 1 s before storage is ready.
- On a first start, an upgrade, or a start with database changes, the app still waits for storage, because storage updates its own tables then.
- I tested this on the packaged Windows app by making storage fail on purpose:

| Case | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Fails once | Retried, Home opened normally |
| Fails twice | Error screen: imports and chat attachments are unavailable |
| Next start | Healthy again |

**About "why it fails":** nothing fails in normal use. Those failures came from a stand-in storage program I wrote so the retry and error paths could be tested. There were no errors in storage, Next.js or backend logs from real starts.

**Owners with many artifacts and bank connections:** the risk doesn't go up for them.
- **Artifacts, accounts, transactions and bank connections** live in the database, which is fully started before the window opens. Storage only holds uploaded statement files and chat attachments.
- **Bank sync:** I found and fixed a real risk here. Bank sync saves each fetched statement into storage, and background jobs were allowed to start before storage was ready. A sync in that gap could have used one of the bank's roughly 4 daily fetches and then failed to save. Bank sync, the scheduler and any interrupted background work now start only once storage is up.
- **What can still hit the gap:** only a statement upload or chat attachment started within about 1 s of the window opening. It would show an error and work on the next try, and nothing gets written.
- **Backups** copy the storage folder straight from disk, so they aren't affected.

**Subagents' leftover work**
- The page-speed agent had 9 finished commits. I merged them as [#322](https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo/pull/322), and all of its CI checks passed before the merge.
- Page JavaScript sizes (KB):

| Page | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ask | 277 | 187 |
| Artifacts | 261 | 168 |
| Settings | 271 | 187 |
| Transactions | 278 | 263 |

- I didn't time those pages; these are bundle sizes, and the size limits were lowered to match.
- The dev-server agent had committed nothing, so there was nothing to add.

**Recording:** #318 now shows two animated recordings of the packaged Windows app, with a timer that starts at the double-click.
- **Reopening:** Home is ready at about 2.5 s, against 6.4 s before.
- **First open after install:** about 25 s, against 17–39 s before.
- **Storage screenshots:** what you see when storage fails once and when it fails twice.

Locally, the unit tests (1,906) and typecheck pass on the final branch.
